messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Text: Spironolactone blocks the effect of male hormones, and male hormones are needed for a male baby to develop normally. In animal studies, male offspring exposed in the womb showed feminized development. The limited information available in humans has not shown a clear increase in birth defects, but the concern remains. Your doctor will usually avoid spironolactone in pregnancy, or talk through the possible risk to a male baby with you. Untreated heart failure, cirrhosis, and high blood pressure also carry real risks in pregnancy, so this is a decision to make with your doctor rather than by stopping on your own.
Breastfeeding:
Spironolactone itself does not pass into breast milk. Its active breakdown product, canrenone, has been found in breast milk in very small amounts that are not expected to affect a breastfed baby. No side effects were reported in the one infant studied over a short period, and the long-term picture is not known. Talk to your doctor so you can weigh this up together.
Children:

The relation 'required for' in the triplet is defined as 'The object entity is necessary for the normal development or function of the subject entity.' Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits.
